plato.population: ITT / full analysis set, all randomized (9333 vs 9291)
plato.source_url: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19717846/ ; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00391872 (results: 399/9333 vs 506/9291) ; https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC5591813 (reproduces NEJM Table: 4.5 vs 5.9, 0.78 (0.69-0.89), P<0.001)
plato.notes: Abstract gives 4.5% vs 5.9%, P<0.001 but no HR; HR/CI confirmed from secondary sources reproducing the NEJM table (PMC5591813, PMC3908913, RxFiles). NEJM full text itself was paywalled (403). ACC summary page misprints CI as 0.69-0.91 (that is the CV-death CI) - ignore.

aristotle.notes: NEJM abstract: 3.52% vs 3.94%/yr, HR 0.89 (0.80-0.99), P=0.047. CT.gov results report the same HR with upper limit 1.00 (P=0.0465) - rounding difference; paper value 0.99 used. Death counts from CT.gov (ITT, intended treatment period to efficacy cutoff 30-Jan-2011).

rocket_af.population: ITT, all randomized (7081 vs 7090), throughout trial incl. post-discontinuation
rocket_af.notes: Paper text: 'in the intention-to-treat analysis throughout the trial, there were 582 deaths in the rivaroxaban group and 632 deaths in the warfarin group (4.5% and 4.9% per year; HR 0.92; 95% CI 0.82-1.03; P=0.15)'. On-treatment (safety, as-treated) result also reported: 208 vs 250 deaths, 1.9% vs 2.2%/yr, HR 0.85 (0.70-1.02), P=0.07 (CT.gov: P=0.073; denominators 7061 vs 7125 on CT.gov, 7061 vs 7082 in paper). ITT is the recommended benchmark.

transform_hf.followup: median 17.4 months (death follow-up up to 30 months)
transform_hf.notes: Confirmed: 373/1431 (26.1%) vs 374/1428 (26.2%), HR 1.02 (0.89-1.18). Open-label, pragmatic; ~4% withdrew consent; crossover/nonadherence noted.

comet.notes: Confirmed: 34% (512/1511) vs 40% (600/1518), HR 0.83 (0.74-0.93), p=0.0017. Metoprolol tartrate target 50 mg bid (lower-dose, short-acting comparator).

ontarget.measure: relative risk (labelled 'risk ratio' in Table 3; time-to-event analysis)
ontarget.population: ITT, all randomized (8542 telmisartan vs 8576 ramipril)
ontarget.notes: Table 3: Death from any cause 1014 (11.8%) ramipril vs 989 (11.6%) telmisartan; telmisartan vs ramipril 0.98 (0.90-1.07). Paper calls it 'relative risk'/'risk ratio'; methods describe time-to-event analysis and hazard ratios (CT.gov reports HRs for other endpoints matching these values), so treat as HR. Combination arm vs ramipril: 1065 deaths, 1.07 (0.98-1.16) - not used.

allhat.measure: RR from Cox proportional hazards model (i.e., HR)
allhat.notes: Table 5: all-cause mortality chlorthalidone 2203 events (6-yr 17.3%), amlodipine 1256 (16.8%); RR 0.96 (0.89-1.02), P=.20. Methods state RRs and CIs were obtained from Cox models. Unequal allocation (~1.7:1 chlorthalidone).

ascot.notes: Abstract: all-cause mortality 738 vs 820; 0.89 (0.81-0.99), p=0.025. HR label 'unadjusted HR' stated explicitly for primary endpoint; same format for mortality. Regimens: amlodipine +/- perindopril vs atenolol +/- bendroflumethiazide.

elite_ii.notes: Confirmed: HR 1.13 (95.7% CI 0.95-1.35), p=0.16; average annual mortality 11.7% vs 10.4%. CI is 95.7% (alpha adjusted for interim looks) - if converting to SE, use z=2.024 not 1.96. Death counts from Lancet text as quoted in PMC59604 review (not seen in abstract).
